questions.subject: legal
questions.title: A majority is not always enough
questions.question: A constitutional referendum wins 54% of the national vote and a majority in only three states. Does the proposal pass? Explain.
answer: No. A successful constitutional referendum requires a national majority and a majority in at least four of the six states. The national requirement is met, but the state requirement is not.

points.text: At least four states required; only three support it

questions.pitfall: Do not treat the national vote alone as sufficient. Territory votes count towards the national total, not a state majority.

questions.subject: legal
questions.title: Representative and responsible government
questions.question: Distinguish representative government from responsible government in the Australian parliamentary system.
answer: Representative government means elected representatives make decisions on behalf of the people. Responsible government means the executive is accountable to parliament; a government must maintain the confidence of the lower house.

questions.subject: legal
questions.title: Checking executive decisions

topics: Democracy, the rule of law and government accountability
Governance issues: viewpoints, consequences and legal alternatives

questions.question: An original practice scenario: an executive agency makes decisions without giving affected people reasons. Parliament proposes mandatory reasons and independent review. Analyse one benefit and one possible limitation, then recommend a response using accountability and fairness.
answer: Mandatory reasons help affected people understand and challenge a decision, improving transparency and procedural fairness. Independent review can identify errors and constrain misuse of executive power. Review can require time and resources and may delay final decisions. One defensible recommendation is reasons plus accessible independent review, with appropriate time limits and funding. This supports accountability and fairness while addressing delay.

points.text: Explains a benefit linked to the scenario
Justifies using accountability/fairness and an implication

questions.subject: legal
questions.title: Ratification and domestic law
questions.question: Does Australia’s ratification of a human rights treaty automatically make every treaty provision enforceable in Australian courts? Explain.
answer: No. Ratification creates international obligations but does not by itself incorporate every provision into Australian domestic law. Existing domestic law may already implement some obligations; otherwise legislation may be needed for domestic legal effect.

points.text: Distinguishes international obligation from domestic enforceability
Explains existing law and/or implementing legislation

questions.pitfall: Do not say ratification has no effect: international obligations and domestic enforceability are different issues.

questions.subject: legal
questions.title: Declaration and treaty
questions.question: Explain one important legal difference between the UDHR and the ICCPR.
answer: The UDHR is a declaration setting out human rights standards; it is not itself a treaty. The ICCPR is a treaty that creates international obligations for states that become parties. This distinction does not mean the UDHR has no legal influence or that a treaty automatically becomes domestic law.

points.text: Correctly identifies the UDHR as a declaration
Correctly identifies the ICCPR as a treaty with obligations for parties
Explains rather than simply names the difference

questions.subject: legal
questions.title: Making a justified recommendation

topics: Analysing an Australian human rights issue

questions.question: Use the supplied fictional proposal. Compare keeping the current process with adding free independent assistance. Recommend one using accessibility and fairness. Identify an implication.
answer: Keeping the process limits additional government spending but leaves a documented access barrier. Free independent assistance could help people understand the form and present relevant information, improving accessibility and fairness. A defensible recommendation is funded assistance, with an eligibility or triage process if resources are limited. This requires funding and service capacity; monitor whether abandoned complaints decrease. Other recommendations can earn credit if justified using the criteria and evidence.

questions.question: The exchange rate rises from US$0.70 to US$0.80 per A$1. A US supplier keeps an item’s price at US$400. Calculate its Australian-dollar price before and after the change, then identify the currency movement.

questions.subject: economics
questions.title: Who benefits from a depreciation?
questions.question: Explain one likely benefit and one likely cost of an Australian-dollar depreciation. State an assumption or limitation.
answer: With foreign-currency prices and other factors held constant, Australian exports become cheaper to overseas buyers, potentially increasing export demand and benefiting exporters. Imports become more expensive in A$, raising costs for importers and consumers. The net effect depends on demand responsiveness, contracts, imported inputs and time lags; an improved trade balance is not automatic.

questions.title: Trace a monetary-policy effect
questions.question: Explain how a rise in interest rates can reduce inflationary pressure through household spending. Identify one reason the effect is not immediate or uniform.
answer: Higher lending rates can increase repayments for borrowers and make new borrowing less attractive. Some households reduce consumption, lowering aggregate demand and demand-driven inflationary pressure. Effects vary because some loans have fixed rates, households differ in debt and savings, and decisions take time. Savers may receive more interest income.

questions.title: Choose a market-entry approach

topics: Domestic and global expansion strategies and modes of entry

questions.question: Using control and financial exposure as criteria, compare a wholly owned outlet with licensing for this business. Recommend an approach.
answer: A wholly owned outlet gives greater control over staff, service and brand presentation but places the $800,000 investment and operating risk on the business. questions.title: Judge a transformation
questions.question: Evaluate the transformation using productivity and employee retention. Recommend one refinement.
answer: Output per worker rises from 20 to 26 units, a 30% increase, suggesting improved productivity. One refinement is staff consultation and targeted training/support, followed by monitoring both productivity and turnover. The before/after data alone do not establish that the new system caused every change.

questions.subject: accounting
questions.title: Straight-line depreciation
questions.question: A non-current asset costs $24,000, has residual value $4,000 and useful life 5 years. Calculate annual straight-line depreciation and carrying amount after two complete years. Ignore GST and impairment.
answer: Annual depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life = (24000 − 4000) ÷ 5 = $4,000.
Accumulated depreciation after two years = $8,000. Carrying amount = 24000 − 8,000 = $16,000.

questions.question: At 30 June, a business owes $1,200 wages for work already performed. Nothing has been recorded for these wages. State the adjusting journal entry and explain the effect on profit and liabilities.

questions.title: Profitability is not the same as liquidity
questions.question: Calculate net profit margin and current ratio. Explain why strong sales do not by themselves prove the business can pay short-term debts.

Sales may be on credit and current assets may include inventory, so timing and composition of assets matter for paying debts.

questions.question: Prove by mathematical induction that 1+2+…+n=n(n+1)/2 for every positive integer n.

questions.title: Analyse a qualified viewpoint

topics: Analysing how language and textual conventions shape meaning

questions.question: Analyse how the original written text presents technology. In your course language, explain the viewpoint and the effect of one contrast. The model below explains the ideas in English so you can check meaning; it is not a model of target-language expression.
answer: The viewpoint is qualified: technology enables contact across distance but may reduce interaction with people nearby. The contrast between bringing distant friends closer and distancing the person beside us highlights this tension. The final sentence places responsibility on how people use technology rather than treating technology as inherently good or bad. In the course language, support the analysis with a relevant phrase, such as “随时…联系”与“不再交谈”.

points.text: Recognises qualified rather than wholly positive/negative viewpoint
Analyses the contrast using a textual detail
Explains responsibility/use in the final sentence
